newsitem.title: USA: U.S. farm trade surplus $2.306 billion in December.
newsitem.headline: U.S. farm trade surplus $2.306 billion in December.

text.p: The U.S. trade surplus in agricultural commodities was $2.306 billion in December, down from the revised $3.173 billion in November, the Commerce Department said Wednesday.

In its monthly trade report, Commerce pegged farm exports at $5.164 billion in December, down from the revised $5.775 billion in November. Imports were $2.858 billion, compared to $2.602 billion the previous month.
The cumulative surplus in farm trade was $26.746 billion for 1996, compared with $25.592 billion for 1995. Ag exports were $59.3 billion in 1996 and imports $32.565 billion.

In December, exports of corn, wheat and soybeans fell. Soybeans were down $234 million to $934 million, corn down $203 million to $689 million and wheat down $110 million to $249 million. Cotton, at $351 million, was up $126 million and rice exports rose to $129 million, up $41 million.

Imports of most products rose. Coffee rose by $47 million to $248 million vegetables and fruits by $162 to total $717 million. Tobacco imports were $82 million, up $15 million. Fish and preparations, at $610 million, was down $8 milion.
